definitions.class: The weekly three-hour class session, Tuesdays 2:35-5:35pm in Evans 4220. The first portion introduces concepts through interpersonal exercises, short lectures, and video; the second portion is often spent in interaction with smaller groups, including your lab. Attendance is required at the first two classes to retain a place in the course or on the waiting list. Because of the heavy experiential orientation, you have to be there to learn — you won't get much out of someone else's notes.
definitions.lab: A mandatory three-hour weekly lab meeting, Tuesdays 6:30-9:30pm, held most weeks of the course. In the Lab you work on your personal learning goals and contribute to creating a learning environment. Experienced facilitators are assigned to the group, but it is not their responsibility to make things happen — it is yours. Lab group meeting times are not to be rescheduled. 'Detached observers' gain relatively little from this course.
definitions.retreat: A mandatory off-campus weekend retreat at Wisdom House, Litchfield CT, Friday-Sunday November 6-8. It provides an immersive learning environment to go more deeply into interpersonal relationships. Without an excused absence from the Office of Student Affairs, it is not possible to miss the retreat and pass the course. No exceptions are made for recruiting trips.
definitions.assignments: Written work type 1. Primarily reflection questions in preparation for class. Must be submitted electronically through Canvas prior to the beginning of class in order to receive credit. Since you may use this material in class activities, you may wish to have a device with you in class to access them. The syllabus does not enumerate individual assignment due dates — watch Canvas.
definitions.reflectionJournal: Written work type 2. A weekly entry helping you reflect on that week's Lab and derive learning from the experience. Each entry answers four week-in-review questions: DO (what happened — 1-3 meaningful moments as 'data points', especially risks taken or considered), REFLECT part 1 (your internal and external responses — what you felt/said/did, what you held back and why, what assumptions you made, how the group responded), REFLECT part 2 (what you are learning about yourself, your impact, group behavior, and how it connects to readings and your learning goal), and APPLY (what's next — what you'll try, what interpersonal risk you want to take). Due 48 hours after the end of Lab, submitted through Canvas. Graded on quality, timeliness, and thoroughness — quality not quantity; the factual summary should be the shortest portion. Only the course faculty and reader-coach read it. You get it back with comments at least once, roughly halfway through the course.
definitions.contract: By enrolling you make an explicit contract to be actively involved, treated as seriously as any other contract, between you, the course faculty, and your fellow classmates. You are expected to attend every class, all Lab meetings and the weekend retreat, to be contributing and punctual, to come fully prepared, and to take risks in service of your own and others' learning.
definitions.gradeLevels: HH: exceptional performance in pushing yourself, takes a lot of risks, one of the key people making the group successful, excellent thoughtful written work. H: high involvement, consistently raises issues and takes risks, thorough and timely on all written work. PR: moderate involvement, may periodically raise issues but doesn't consistently take risks, adequate and timely written work. P: low involvement — taking one 'big risk' in one session is a P, not PR — inadequate and untimely written work. F: cumulative result of absence and non-involvement, significant missing written work, doing the bare minimum.
definitions.attendancePenalty: Missing class, a Lab session, or being late for several classes drops your grade down one level, for each absence. Several LATE arrivals count as an absence.
definitions.notTherapy: Although the course can be intense and at times involves strong emotions, it is not therapy. It deals with interpersonal issues, not intrapersonal. If you are in therapy, check the advisability of taking this course with your therapist.

gradingPolicy: One third of the grade is the quality of your written work (Assignments & Reflection Journal); one third is your personal risk-taking in the Lab; one third is the extent to which you help the group develop and others learn. At the end of the semester you evaluate your own risk-taking and peers evaluate your contributions to the lab; this is combined with faculty impressions and facilitator input. Penalties for tardiness and absences are then deducted. Missing class, a Lab session, or being late for several classes drops your grade one level per absence. Yale SOM Grading Policy: http://portal.som.yale.edu/page/grading-policy
